summary: A three-day marine science program for 18 students and 2 chaperones in Key Largo, combining classroom learning, two-stop reef snorkels with fish surveys, and a guided mangrove tour at Pennekamp.

days.title: Become a Citizen Scientist
days.theme: Arrive at REEF, learn the survey method, then put it to work on the reef.

blocks.title: Arrival at REEF
blocks.description: Your group arrives at the REEF campus in Key Largo. REEF educators welcome the group and preview the days ahead.

blocks.title: Citizen Science Introduction
blocks.description: At the REEF campus, students learn how REEF's citizen scientists identify and record the fish of the Florida Keys and how those fish are adapted to life on the reef. They try a mock fish survey and make a Gyotaku fish print.

blocks.title: Lunch (on your own)
blocks.description: Lunch is not included in this proposal. Your group can bring lunch or pick up food nearby.

blocks.title: Two-Stop Reef Snorkel & Fish Surveys
blocks.description: Students board a boat to two Key Largo coral reef sites and snorkel, recording the fish they find with the Volunteer Fish Survey Project (VFSP) method. Snorkel gear is included. Boat times are confirmed once your dates are set.

blocks.title: Dinner (on your own)
blocks.description: Dinner is not included in this proposal. Your group arranges dinner on its own.

studentsWill: Learn what REEF is and how citizen scientists protect reefs.
Practice a fish survey and make a Gyotaku fish print.
Snorkel two reef sites and record the fish they find.
days.outcomesNote: Times are planning times. Boat times are confirmed once your dates are set.

days.title: Level Up Your Fish ID
days.theme: Snorkel again, investigate lionfish, and test your fish ID skills.

blocks.title: Two-Stop Reef Snorkel & Fish Surveys
blocks.description: Students board a boat to two Key Largo coral reef sites and snorkel, recording the fish they find with the Volunteer Fish Survey Project (VFSP) method. Snorkel gear is included. Boat times are confirmed once your dates are set.

blocks.title: Lunch (on your own)
blocks.description: Lunch is not included in this proposal. Your group can bring lunch or pick up food nearby.

blocks.title: Invasive Species: Lionfish Lesson & Dissection
blocks.description: Students investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection, looking at anatomy and adaptations and learning why lionfish are a conservation challenge for Florida Keys reefs.

blocks.title: Level 2 Fish ID Exam
blocks.description: Students review Caribbean fish identification and take the Level 2 exam toward becoming a REEF Level 2 surveyor.

blocks.title: Dinner (on your own)
blocks.description: Dinner is not included in this proposal. Your group arranges dinner on its own.

studentsWill: Record a second set of reef fish surveys.
Investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection.
Take the Level 2 fish ID exam.
days.outcomesNote: Times are planning times. Boat times are confirmed once your dates are set.

days.title: One Big Reef: Ecology
days.theme: Study how a reef ecosystem fits together, then explore the mangroves.

blocks.title: Florida Keys Ecology & Mangrove Making
blocks.description: A Florida Keys ecology lesson on how reefs, seagrass and mangroves connect and depend on each other, followed by a hands-on mangrove-making activity.

blocks.title: Grouper Moon: Endangered Species Lesson & Role Play
blocks.description: Students learn about Nassau grouper and other threatened and endangered marine species of the Florida Keys, why they are at risk, and what people are doing to protect them. A role play puts students in the shoes of the people who decide how to protect them.

blocks.title: Lunch (on your own)
blocks.description: Lunch is not included in this proposal. Your group can bring lunch or pick up food nearby.

blocks.title: Kayaking at Pennekamp (Mangrove Tour)
blocks.description: A guided REEF tropical ecology tour of the mangroves at John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, with kayaks and park entrance included.

studentsWill: Explain how reefs, seagrass and mangroves depend on each other.
Learn why Nassau grouper and other species need protection.
Explore a mangrove ecosystem on a guided tour.
days.outcomesNote: Times are planning times. Boat times are confirmed once your dates are set.
